title: Neo-Noir
description: Neo-noir cinematography keeps noir's hard keys and isolated blocking but replaces silver night with color: sodium vapor, neon practicals, and tungsten that stain rain and skin. The camera still hunts faces in shadow, yet the palette is contemporary, often cyan signage against warm flesh, not black-and-white contrast alone.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: The city is still a trap, but the trap has a hue. Rain carries magenta and cyan.
A sodium streetlamp turns a raincoat mustard. The moral geometry (half a face, a wet street, a figure stranded in a pool of light) survives.
Only the stock is color. It is the wrong tool when you need period silver, future screens as the only keys, or candy primaries as threat.
Classic Film Noir has no neon to name. Tech Noir puts crime inside a digital city.
Vaporwave uses pink-cyan without guilt or investigation.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Keep a hard key 45 to 90 degrees off, but let practical color do the fill: neon in rain, sodium overhead, a tungsten interior leaking onto wet asphalt. Contrast stays high.
Skin may go teal-shadow, orange-highlight, or stay mixed on purpose. Lens: 35mm or 40mm anamorphic, or spherical 35mm, often at night with rain as the volume.
Camera: locked wides, slow tracking, occasional push-in on a face. Prompt color where classic noir was silver, name the neon practicals, and keep the rain.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it when a present-day or period-color crime scene needs melancholy and rain, not a 1940s silver print. Do not use it as a teal-and-orange grade on a scene with no hard key and no guilty blocking.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: Neo-Noir is color noir: same isolation, new practicals. Film Noir is the silver original.
Tech Noir adds science-fiction production design and screens as sources. Teal and Orange is a grade, not a genre look; you can grade a comedy teal-orange and still have no noir blocking.
Neon Practicals is the lamp. Neo-noir is the lamp plus the crime geometry.

blocks.text: Chinatown (period color, hard sun and venetian interiors, investigation as a trap). Blade Runner (rain, smoke, neon as key, still a detective picture).
Drive (night exteriors, pink-cyan practicals, locked-off melancholy). Grammar, not frames to copy.

sections.title: Prompt it

blocks.text: Neo-noir look on [Subject], color where classic noir was silver, neon practicals, rain, contemporary crime blocking, hard key, unfilled far cheek. Name the hue of the signage and whether the camera is locked or tracking.
Do not write only teal and orange.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is Film Noir (you asked for color and got a black-and-white fedora) or a Teal and Orange grade with no key. The tell is a filled, even night or a palette with no motivated practical.
Fix: add a named neon or sodium source, keep the hard ratio, and wet the ground.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Neo-Noir in film?
Noir themes and blocking restaged after color: hard keys, rain, isolation, and crime, lit by sodium, neon, and tungsten instead of silver nitrate night.
Neo-Noir vs Film Noir

Film noir withholds with black-and-white contrast and tungsten gobos. Neo-noir withholds with color practicals. Same guilty geometry, different stock. If the frame has no hue you can name, it is not neo-noir.
When should I use Neo-Noir?
When a color crime scene needs rain, neon, and a face half in shadow. Skip it for 1940s silver, for future-corporate screens (Tech Noir), or for pastel mall nostalgia (Vaporwave).
How do I prompt Neo-Noir for AI image or video?

Write: Neo-noir look on [Subject], color where classic noir was silver, neon practicals, rain, hard key, unfilled cheek, contemporary crime blocking. Name cyan or magenta signage. Do not stop at a teal-orange slider.
